outputs: coverage_matrix.json maps 24 planned modules, 63 feature-to-case entries, 8 release acceptance criteria and 45 v0.1 test files; states are covered, pending_same_batch, documentation_only or future_gate

the matrix validator resolves every referenced file::test node with AST, requires non-empty test files for covered modules, keeps old test files present, and checks the 29-tool catalog, entry points, import paths and the original mock query

evidence_floor.json requires at least 1600 passing cases, no more than 5% skips, Node results, dev-results side-effect counters, coverage-matrix test files and the Linux 3.12/3.13 plus Windows 3.12 Python matrix
Linux tests use the real file-key backend: 0600 mode, broad permission refusal, symlink refusal, key/data separation, tamper detection and ciphertext without plaintext
Windows tests use the real DPAPI backend and are skipped on Linux with an explicit platform reason; no Windows host result is claimed from the Linux run

the seven-fault matrix covers timeout, lost/cut response, cancellation, lock conflict, process exit, disk full and partial write; every write path has request counters and no uncertain write is replayed
the timeout case uses a threading.Event barrier; the test waits until the facade has entered before releasing it, so a slow runner cannot make the call-count assertion race
protected-store rotation interruption, pointer-switch failure, ENOSPC, short write and fsync failure keep the previous verified record readable; no temporary file is adopted as a record
lost upload response keeps upload count at one across repeated result reads; prepare sends zero remote writes; a lost submit is resolved by readback, not resend
cursor, cache, media reference and dashboard session are bound to account and scope; cross-account and cross-semester use is refused instead of returning old data

cross-midnight intervals keep their exact start/end and Asia/Shanghai timezone; date-only deadlines stay DATE and never receive midnight; stable ids survive title changes and separate same-title sources
a failed source produces SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE with historical carry-forward and zero DELETED; a missing page produces SOURCE_INCOMPLETE and suppresses deletion; neither becomes an empty success

report generator fields: schema, source commit/branch/dirty, product version, contract inventory and set digest, platform/Python/Node/CI identity, scope, totals, Node totals, module buckets, skip reasons, gaps, failures and side-effect source plus counters

failure records contain only the node id, module, stable error class and a pytest minimal repro; name, file, classname and skip reasons are path/token sanitized; raw exception text, paths, tokens, cookies and account values never enter the report
skip classification is an explicit registry with platform:/env: prefixes; Pillow/WebP capability gaps are environment, macOS-only reasons are platform, and an unregistered reason fails the gate

aggregate requires the requested platforms (linux and windows by default), one source commit, matching product versions, matching contract-set digests and a declared platform that agrees with the host and CI runner; dirty or commitless reports fail
evidence floor: empty, one-case, all-skipped, filtered, node-less, dev-results-less and coverage-incomplete suites do not pass

release gate requires test evidence, scans source and every candidate archive with privacy_scan, audits the frozen runtime/dev/Node pins from one distribution manifest, checks conservative defaults, verifies the candidate and scans every archive for the exact marker set while skipping only the committed marker definition file
privacy_scan has a POSIX user-path rule for the home/Users user segment; synthetic test users are allowlisted, real users are not

CI test jobs emit per-platform JUnit, build and upload only safe regression-report JSON, and the release-gate job downloads all platform reports, builds the candidate, runs the gate with marker_set.json, --expected-commit and --require-python-matrix and uploads release-gate.json

CI uses fixed Ubuntu 24.04 / Windows 2025, Python 3.12/3.13, Node 24, explicit Chromium installation split by platform, 60/40 minute job timeouts, read-only contents permission, persist-credentials false and no pull_request_target; actions are pinned to 40-character commit SHAs
docs/MAINTENANCE.md documents report, aggregate and release-gate commands, required markers, evidence floor, commit/platform binding, skip semantics and the Ubuntu-only candidate build

evidence_floor.json enforces a minimum pass count, skip ratio, Node evidence, dev-results evidence and coverage-matrix test files; empty, one-case, all-skipped and filtered suites fail.
load_markers returns (markers, error); missing, unreadable or empty marker sets fail the release gate; an empty marker set makes the archive scan return NO_MARKERS instead of ok.

The local API timeout case uses an event barrier and a 0.5 s deadline; the worker thread may outlive the request until the service stops, which is the 6.2 documented process boundary, not a new cancellation capability.

The report keeps only error classes and repository-relative node ids. Skip reasons and findings are path/token sanitized, but the report is an engineering summary, not a general data-loss-prevention system.
